health_map_descriptions.analyzing: Your site is currently undergoing a detailed analysis to assess its security posture and pinpoint potential vulnerabilities or threats. This review encompasses a thorough evaluation of your site's infrastructure, codebase, and operational protocols.
health_map_descriptions.atRisk: Your site is currently at risk. We've identified low severity vulnerabilities or malware, such as comment spam or SEO spam. These issues could potentially allow attackers to alter or inject content on your site. Additionally, incomplete product configuration may limit the protection SiteLock offers. Address these low severity concerns promptly to prevent further infections and enhance your site's security.
health_map_descriptions.compromised: Your site has been flagged as Compromised due to significant security breaches that have been detected. This status indicates a severe vulnerability in your site's security posture, leading to unauthorized access or damage. Immediate and comprehensive action is required to mitigate these risks, prevent further data loss, and safeguard your site's integrity.
health_map_descriptions.healthy: Your site is in excellent condition! We've detected no malware, vulnerabilities, or configuration issues. You're fully protected, and your web environment is secure. Keep up the good work to maintain your site's health and ensure ongoing security.
health_map_descriptions.impaired: Your website's security is impaired due to moderate severity vulnerabilities and/or malware. These threats could grant attackers access to parts of your files or database, enabling them to inject unwanted content. While not in full control, this level of compromise needs immediate attention. Act quickly to secure your site and prevent escalation.
health_map_descriptions.unavailable: Your site's health status is currently unavailable as no security scans have been initiated or no subscriptions are active. Please initiate a scan or subscribe to our services to activate this feature and start monitoring your site's security health.
health_map_descriptions.requiresActivation: Connect your free SiteLock account to unlock real-time site health reports, vulnerability scans, and proactive protection tools.

cloud_services_description.advisories: The Risk Score is an aggregated security score sourced from both SiteLock reports as well as external security scans reporting your website reputation. This is a great source of information on what changes can be made to improve your website's security standing for the better!
cloud_services_description.backup: It's important to back your website up before any updates (like plugins or themes) so you have an option in case there are complications. It's always important to have a backup of your website in the event of a malware attack, as it gives you the ability to restore a backup and restore functionality to your website quickly.
cloud_services_description.patchman: SMART Patch continuously detects the vulnerabilities in your website and is able to safely patch them.
cloud_services_description.scanning: Security scanning is the process of using automated tools to identify vulnerabilities, risks, and weaknesses in systems, networks, or applications. It helps prevent attacks by detecting potential security flaws early.
cloud_services_description.spam_scan: While SiteLock is a website security company, it's important to be aware of your website's email reputation. Being blacklisted by email security vendors can lead to your emails being silently rejected by recipients who use those security vendors.
cloud_services_description.ssl_scan: Make sure your website visitors feel safe when visiting and interacting with your website by ensuring your SSL is properly configured. Not only will this make website visitors trust your website more, but it will make search engines like Google trust you more too!
cloud_services_description.waf: Implementing a website firewall solution is a proactive way to prevent hackers from installing malicious code onto your website. This technology provides advanced protection by automatically addressing vulnerabilities to help keep your site users safe. Start blocking advanced web attacks in seconds with SiteLock’s WAF cloud security services.

security_scan_description.databaseScan: Scan your database for common spam terms as well as malicious code or bad URLs intended to hurt the reputation of your website.
security_scan_description.fileScan: Take advantage of a growing database of known malware signatures to ensure that if malware finds its way into your files, it's promptly removed!
security_scan_description.vulnerabilityScan: Check the integrity of your CMS plugins, themes, and extensions so you know when updates are needed. These updates are critical to your website security!
security_scan_description.webpageScan: The Webpage Scan uses PhishTank, Anti-Virus Blacklist and our own SiteLock service to look for malware on your publicly facing website.

security_enhancements_list.limitPhpExecution: Deny Access to Unsafe Script Extensions

security_enhancements_description.forceHttps: Force HTTPS ensures all website traffic is encrypted by redirecting HTTP requests to HTTPS. This enhances security by protecting data from interception and boosts SEO rankings. It can be implemented through server configurations (Apache), CMS settings (WordPress), or CDN features (Cloudflare), and is often paired with HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) for added protection.
security_enhancements_description.disableDirectoryListing: Disable Directory Listing prevents the display of files in a directory when there is no index file (like index.html or index.php). It enhances security by hiding the contents of directories from unauthorized users, reducing the risk of exposing sensitive files. This can be configured via server settings (Apache, Nginx) or through .htaccess rules.
security_enhancements_description.limitPhpExecution: This restricts the execution of PHP scripts to specific files and directories, significantly reducing the risk of attackers running malicious scripts on your server. By limiting PHP execution to only necessary files, such as those within the WordPress core or theme/plugin directories, this measure helps block unauthorized or harmful code from being executed, even if uploaded to your site.
security_enhancements_description.xssSqliProtection: Basic XSS & SQLi Protection prevents malicious attacks by sanitizing user input. XSS protection blocks harmful scripts in the browser, while SQLi protection uses prepared statements and input validation to secure database queries, safeguarding against unauthorized access and data manipulation.
security_enhancements_description.hardenWritableDirs: Prevent PHP execution inside writable directories (like /wp-content/uploads), which should only contain static assets. This helps stop attackers from running malicious code through uploaded files.

website_security_enhancements_list.limitPhpExecution: Deny Access to Unsafe Script Extensions

website_security_enhancements_descriptio.disableDirectoryListing: Prevent unauthorized access to directory contents
website_security_enhancements_descriptio.limitPhpExecution: Block execution of files with unsafe extensions (phtml, phar, cgi, pl, py, asp, aspx, jsp) in the WordPress root to prevent malicious scripts from running.
website_security_enhancements_descriptio.xssSqliProtection: Guard against cross-site scripting and SQL injection attacks
website_security_enhancements_descriptio.hardenWritableDirs: Prevent PHP execution inside writable directories (like /wp-content/uploads), which should only contain static assets. This helps stop attackers from running malicious code through uploaded files.

login_security_description.2FA: 2FA (Two-Factor Authentication) adds an extra layer of security by requiring two forms of verification: something you know (password) and something you have (like a mobile device or authenticator app), making it harder for unauthorized users to access accounts.
login_security_description.loginLockout: The Login Lockout feature protects your site from brute-force attacks by limiting failed login attempts. If a user exceeds the maximum allowed attempts, their IP is temporarily locked out.
login_security_description.passwordStrengthToolandEnforcement: The Password Strength Tool and Enforcement feature ensures that users create strong passwords by evaluating their complexity. It enforces password policies, requiring a mix of characters, length, and unpredictability to enhance security against unauthorized access.
login_security_description.forceLogoutByTimePeriod: Enforce a fixed logout time for selected roles to reduce the risk of unauthorized access. This setting disables the 'Remember me' option on login.

two_factor_authentication_settings_steps.description: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of protection to your WordPress login by requiring a second step – like a code from your phone – in addition to your password. Use the options below to set up 2FA for your own account.
two_factor_authentication_settings_steps.twofaMessage: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of protection to your WordPress login by requiring a second step – like a code from your phone – in addition to your password.
two_factor_authentication_settings_steps.confirmDisable: Are you sure you want to disable Two-Factor Authentication? This will immediately reduce the security of your account, leaving it protected by only your password.
two_factor_authentication_settings_steps.confirmMessage: We strongly recommend keeping Two-Factor Authentication enabled for maximum account security.

stepOne.title: Step 1. Scan Code
stepOne.description: Scan the QR code below using your preferred authenticator app (like Google Authenticator, Authy, or Microsoft Authenticator) to add this account. You can enter the setup key manually instead if required.
stepOne.copyManually: Copy this code and enter it manually into your authenticator app:

stepTwo.title: Step 2. Enter 2FA Code
stepTwo.description: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app and click “Verify & Activate”.

stepThree.title: Step 3. Save Recovery Codes
stepThree.description: Use these one-time backup codes if you lose access to your authenticator app.
stepThree.storeCodes: Store these codes in a safe place.
stepThree.enabled_line1: You have successfully enabled two-factor authentication for your account.
stepThree.enabled_line2: From now on, you'll be asked to enter a verification code from your app when logging in.
activationSteps: Two-Factor Authentication is currently enabled for your account.
You are required to enter a verification code from your authenticator app when logging in.

Your one-time backup codes were generated during this activation process. These codes are tied to your current configuration. If you click the Disable button, all current 2FA settings and these backup codes will be permanently deleted. You must then re-enable 2FA to generate a new set of codes.
stepThree.recoveryCodeNoticeLine1: Your recovery codes will only be accessible for the next ##remaining-time##. After that, they will be #b#permanently deleted#/b# for security reasons. We strongly recommend storing them in a #b#secure location#/b# (e.g., a password manager or encrypted file) before they disappear.

2fa.title: 2FA (Two Factor Authentication)
2fa.description: Add an extra layer of protection to user logins by requiring a one-time code in addition to the password.
2fa.disableRoleInfo: * This role is disabled because it lacks the required permissions to access the WordPress dashboard.
2fa.enabledRoles: Choose which user roles must use 2FA.
2fa.gracePeriodDescription: Give users extra time to set up 2FA before it becomes mandatory. After the grace period ends, users must enable 2FA to log in.

2fa_disable_modal.title: Disable 2FA?
2fa_disable_modal.description: Are you sure you want to disable Two-Factor Authentication? This action is highly discouraged and will immediately reduce the security on your site.
2fa_disable_modal.message: If you proceed, the following destructive changes will occur:
disableFactors: All saved 2FA settings for every user (keys and backup codes) will be permanently deleted.
All users who previously logged in using 2FA will no longer be required to provide a second authentication factor.
Users will need to re-enable and reconfigure 2FA if this setting is turned back on later.
2fa_disable_modal.confirmationLabel: Please type the word DISABLE to confirm

login_lockout.title: Login Lockout
login_lockout.description: Temporarily block users after repeated failed login attempts.
login_lockout.maxLoginDescription: Number of failed login attempts allowed before the account is blocked.
login_lockout.lockoutDescription: How long the accounts stays locked after reaching the maximum attempts.
login_lockout.resetTimeDescription: If no failed attempts occur during this time, the attempt counter resets.

force_logouts.title: Force Logouts
force_logouts.description: Enforce a fixed logout time for selected roles to reduce the risk of unauthorized access. This setting disables the 'Remember me' option on login.
force_logouts.excludeRolesDescription: Choose roles that are not affected by force logouts.
force_logouts.timePeriodDescription: Maximum length of a login session before the user is logged out.

password_strength_enforcement.title: Password Strength Enforcement
password_strength_enforcement.description: Require users to create secure passwords to help protect accounts from brute-force attacks. Enforcement applies only to new user registrations and password changes.
password_strength_enforcement.minimumStrengthDescription: Choose the minimum required password strength for each role, or disable enforcement.

login_activity_log.title: Login Activity Log
login_activity_log.description: Record all user logins for security monitoring and troubleshooting.
login_activity_log.loginRetentionPeriodDescription: Delete login records older than the selected period.

login_security_list_settings.title: Login Security
login_security_list_settings.description: Protect your WordPress site from unauthorized access with these essential login security tools. Configure two-factor authentication, enforce strong passwords, monitor login activity, and apply other safeguards to help secure your admin area.
